doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

title: Musicians taught him to write about them
summary: Liner notes, WBAI radio and musicians correcting his writing; poets and painters like Baudelaire and Manet, and Baraka.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Did you ever have an occasion where you wrote about a musician and made some opinions of your own, perhaps some assumptions, and then heard from that musician saying, “I was not thinking that” or “that was not my intention?”
It happened with liner notes all the time because I always showed them the notes before I turned them in.

And they’d make corrections on them, yes. Yeah I think this thing about, incidentally the thing I want to diverge from your question a bit but it’s related, this thing about artists, about poets learning to write about art forms from the artists themselves. I mean it’s a similar kind of thing that came up and again, going back to, I thought of this when I started talking about Montmartre. If you look at the early Impressionists, it wasn’t the academic critics who wrote about Manet for example. Baudelaire was Manet’s critic and if you look at the Impressionists it was always the poets who wrote the reviews not because the Academy was adamantly opposed to this it was Apollinaire who wrote about Matisse. And they were great friends. They went out and they chased women together, they got drunk together, but basically Matisse taught Apollinaire how to write about his art. So I think that is what happened with LeRoi Jones, Amiri Baraka and me. We were hanging out with the musicians and they basically taught us how to write about them, not formally but you know we learned in conversation and listening to them and watching them work.
